name: THE BARBER'S
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE TRAY
LOOK_AT: Instruments. I have identified the razor. I am choosing not to identify the others.
Laid out in a row from small to alarming. The razor is at the small end, which is the only comfort the tray offers.
Everything on it has been cleaned. I can tell, because it has been cleaned the way you clean something you've used.
LISTEN_TO: Steel settling on cloth when I lean on the shelf.
Nothing. I've stepped back. That will do.

overrides.PICK_UP: I'd rather the instruments stayed with a man who knows which is which.

subjects.name: THE CHAIR
LOOK_AT: One chair, for shaves, teeth and limbs alike. The arms have straps. I'm told the straps are for the teeth.
There is a bucket beside it. The bucket is for the teeth, I hope.
It reclines with a lever. Every man who has sat in it has learned the word 'reclines' the hard way.
LISTEN_TO: The leather creaking as it settles. It has heard every kind of language a man knows.
A spring, deep inside, sighing at the very idea of me.
Nothing. It's waiting with the patience of a thing that always gets its man.

overrides.USE: I'd sit in it, but he'd take it as a request.

subjects.name: THE STROP
LOOK_AT: A leather strop on a hook, polished to a mirror down the middle by ten thousand strokes.
Two straps, one canvas, one leather. Canvas first, then leather. He showed me, though I hadn't asked.
The leather is darker where his hand holds it. He has stood in exactly that place for years.
LISTEN_TO: It swings a little when the door goes, and slaps the chair once, like a reminder.
Nothing. The strop is between shaves, like the rest of us.

overrides.PULL: It pulls back. Strops do. I let go before it made a point of it.

subjects.name: THE JAR
LOOK_AT: A jar on the shelf, which I am not going to look in. I have decided.
I looked in the jar. I'd like to go back to not having looked in the jar.
The jar. I know what's in it now, and the jar knows I know.
LISTEN_TO: A faint clink from inside when the floor moves. I'm not going to think about what clinks.
I'm not listening to the jar any more. The jar has had enough of my attention.

overrides.OPEN: No. I have looked in the jar. I am not going in the jar.

subjects.name: THE MIRROR
LOOK_AT: A mirror, with a crack running across it at about the height of a nervous man's chin.
Me, in a barber's mirror, looking like a man who needs a shave and is going to think about it first.
The crack goes right through my reflection's neck. I've decided not to read anything into it.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The mirror keeps its opinions on its face.
Nothing. It's turned to the wall a little, as if it had seen enough.
Nothing. Mirrors are the only thing in Consolation that never argue.

subjects.name: THE PRICE BOARD
LOOK_AT: SHAVE 2 BITS. TOOTH 4 BITS. LIMB $1. The limb is the bargain, which worries me.
No price for a haircut. Either it's free, or he doesn't do them, and I'm afraid to find out which.
Someone has scratched a name under LIMB, and then scratched it out again. I hope he kept the limb.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The prices speak for themselves, and loudly.
The board tapping against the wall in the draft: two bits, four bits, a dollar.
Nothing. It's said its prices. It doesn't haggle.
